_comment: Crop requirements for Tanzanian growing conditions. Data only - no business logic. Keys are the canonical crop names used by app.ai.features.CROP_PROFILE, which is the system's own crop list. minimum_rain_mm / ideal_rain_mm are totals for one season, not per day. Extending the system with a new crop means adding it to CROP_PROFILE first, then here.

maize.note: Needs a reliable supply through tasselling; a dry spell then heavy rain costs more yield than steady rain.

rice.note: Needs standing water or very reliable irrigation, so it is a wet-season crop.

beans.note: A short 90-day crop that fits the shoulder months between the two rainy seasons.

sorghum.note: Tolerates heat and a dry spell better than maize, which makes it the safer dry-season choice.

cassava.note: A long dry-season crop that stores water in the root and is harvested after 8 or 9 months.

wheat.note: A cool-season crop; it is planted in the dry season on residual moisture and does not tolerate heat.

groundnut.note: A legume that fixes its own nitrogen, so it suits poor soils and a shorter rainfall window.

cotton.note: Needs a long frost-free window and a dry finish so the bolls open.

vegetables.note: The most irrigation-hungry crop in the list and the most sensitive to heat; best close to water.

planting_window._comment: Rule-based scoring for the best stretch to plant into. A day is penalised for too little rain, too much rain, extreme heat and strong wind; a run of days is scored by its average penalty, and the lowest-scoring run wins. Weights are deliberately simple so the reason can be explained to the farmer.

history._comment: Minimum stored data before a season-vs-history percentage is reported at all. Below this the advisory omits the comparison instead of inventing one.
